summary: The hypothesis that a faster multi-cell greedy initialization would improve simulated annealing (SA) scores was refuted. Both arms scored in the 88–91 range (h-main mean 89.92, h-ablation mean 89.38), with a difference of only +0.54 points — well within the ~5-point run-to-run variance from different random test cases. SA dominates final score quality regardless of initialization method.
key_points: h-main (multi-cell init + SA) scored 88.71, 90.65, 90.39 (mean 89.92); h-ablation (single-cell init + SA) scored 88.88, 88.82, 90.45 (mean 89.38) — the +0.54 difference is not statistically meaningful given judge variance.

The directional prediction (multi-cell init > single-cell init) failed in 2 of 3 runs, confirming that initialization quality is not a bottleneck — SA converges to similar solutions from either starting point.

Two iterations have now established that SA is the dominant scoring mechanism (~88–91 range). Further gains likely require changes to SA neighborhood structure, cooling schedule, or a fundamentally different representation — not init improvements.
